job.title: Credit Controller
job.description:
Credit Controller
Role: Credit Controller
Salary: Up to £48,000
Location: London
Contract: Permanent

Are you an experienced Credit Controller from a law firm or professional services background looking for your next step with a firm that genuinely invests in its people? A highly regarded City law firm, known for advising on some of the most complex and demanding mandates in the market, is looking to add a Credit Controller to its Finance department. This is a newly created position resulting from growth, offering the chance to join a collaborative, supportive team where your contribution will be recognised.

The Role
Sitting within a well established Revenue team and reporting to the Head of Revenue, the Credit Controller will take a proactive approach to supporting collections across the firm. This is a busy and varied role covering large client group debts, a portfolio of aged debts and the monitoring of legal proceedings on unrecoverable debts, as well as complex billing matters, all working towards the firm's cash collection targets. The firm places real emphasis on learning and development, so you will be supported to keep building your skills. Key responsibilities include:
  • Proactively chasing a portfolio of large client group debts to ensure prompt settlement of invoices, including preparing client statements in line with the credit control procedure
  • Organising and attending regular debt meetings with Partners
  • Managing an aged debt portfolio of debts over one year old
  • Taking ownership of issues and queries around unpaid invoices, escalating where necessary, monitoring progress and pursuing until resolved
  • Processing invoice write offs in line with the firm's policies and VAT rules
  • Maintaining a full log of credit control notes and status within the collections application
  • Producing regular debt reports to identify issues for escalation
  • Working with Revenue Controllers to resolve complex debt issues
  • Liaising regularly with Cashiers on the allocation of unapplied or unidentified monies and investigating any errors
  • Where required, preparing and monitoring files for debt recovery on debts deemed unrecoverable
  • Supporting and mentoring junior members of the team, fostering a collaborative, high performance environment
The Candidate
We are looking for someone with:
  • Three to five years' credit control experience, ideally within a law firm, although professional services backgrounds will also be considered
  • Exposure to VAT, disbursements and credit control, with the ability to hit the ground running in a target driven environment
  • Knowledge of Aderant and HighRadius (or other collections software), which would be advantageous
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience of liaising with clients, partners, fee earners, secretaries and finance colleagues
  • A proactive, organised and professional manner, comfortable dealing with stakeholders at all levels of the business
  • A team player who supports and motivates colleagues, follows instructions and is confident to query them when unsure
  • A clear track record of commitment to the highest level of customer service
  • A high level of numeracy and a good understanding of financial workings
  • A keen eye for detail and a solution focused approach, able to act positively, creatively and intuitively when presented with challenges
Interested to be considered or to find out more? Please apply now or contact Becky Bradley at Balance Recruitment (beckybradley@balancerecruitment.com) to discuss further. Don't worry if you don't have your CV together yet, we can help with that.

job.title: VAT Manager
job.description:
Role: VAT Manager
Salary: Up to £100,000
Location: London, in office 3 days p/wk
Contract: Permanent

Are you an experienced VAT or indirect tax compliance professional looking for a role where you can take genuine end to end ownership, rather than just being one part of a bigger process? A well established international law firm is expanding its London based indirect tax operations capability, and is looking for a VAT Manager to take charge of its day to day compliance activity across multiple jurisdictions.

The Role
Reporting to the Indirect Tax Operations Manager, the VAT Manager will own the day to day delivery of the firm's indirect tax compliance activities across multiple jurisdictions, including Europe, Asia Pacific, and the Middle East. This is a hands on role with real scope for ownership, sitting within a growing Indirect Tax Operations Team and working closely with Finance, Billing, Accounting, Accounts Payable, Financial Systems, local office personnel, and external advisors. You will also supervise and develop a VAT Analyst, giving you a genuine management dimension alongside the technical work. Key responsibilities include:
  • Managing preparation, review, and submission of VAT/GST returns across applicable jurisdictions.
  • Managing European Sales Listings, Intrastat filings, and other periodic indirect tax reporting obligations.
  • Owning the firm's VAT compliance calendar and ensuring filing deadlines and submission requirements are met.
  • Reviewing supporting workpapers, account reconciliations, data extracts, and compliance documentation prepared by the VAT Analyst or external advisors.
  • Monitoring VAT legislative and administrative developments and coordinating implementation of required filing or process updates.
  • Managing recurring interactions with external VAT advisors and service providers, and coordinating responses to tax authority inquiries and VAT audits.
  • Leading, supervising, and mentoring the VAT Analyst, setting priorities and delivering technical coaching on filings, reconciliations, and documentation.
  • Supporting e invoicing and real time reporting initiatives, and contributing to process documentation, compliance playbooks, and control improvements.
  • Supporting VAT registrations, deregistrations, and changes to existing registrations as the firm's obligations evolve.
The Candidate
We are looking for someone with:
  • 8+ years of VAT or indirect tax compliance experience, ideally within a multinational organisation, professional services firm, or law firm environment.
  • Strong practical knowledge of VAT/GST returns, European Sales Listings, Intrastat reporting, VAT registrations, and related compliance requirements.
  • Experience managing multi jurisdictional filing obligations and advisor relationships.
  • Experience supporting VAT audits, tax authority inquiries, or compliance reviews.
  • Strong Excel and data management skills, and comfort working with large datasets and reconciliations.
  • Excellent organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple deadlines and competing priorities across jurisdictions.
  • A proactive and solutions oriented approach, with the confidence to take ownership of day to day compliance activities and drive issues through to resolution.
  • The ability to supervise and develop less experienced team members.
  • Interest in e invoicing, tax technology, automation, and process improvement initiatives.
  • ATT, CTA, ACA, ACCA, or equivalent qualification, or progress toward qualification, is preferred but not essential.

job.title: Revenue Controller - London
job.description:
A leading international law firm is looking to hire a Revenue Controller into its London based finance team.

This is a role for someone who enjoys being close to the commercial engine of a firm, working with Partners and matter teams to keep billing on track, manage receivables, and drive timely cash collection across a busy portfolio.

From day one, you will sit in the space between fee earners and finance. You will build strong working relationships with Partners and matter managers, meeting regularly to review WIP and AR, agreeing clear next steps and making sure actions do not drift.

The role is as much about pace and influence as it is about process. You will be expected to bring structure, keep stakeholders informed, and move matters forward with confidence and professionalism.

Billing is a core part of the role. You will draft and finalise invoices in line with firm policy and regulatory requirements, ensure the right documentation is filed, and keep a close eye on WIP so billing happens at the right time with accurate narratives, rates and coding. You will also support fee updates and respond quickly when clients require specific formats, supporting information, or tighter timelines.

On the collections side, you will stay close to aged debt, agree action plans with Partners, and assist with collections for your stakeholder group. Where needed, you will work with central credit control support, but you will remain accountable for progress and communication. You will also keep the ledgers clean by reviewing unallocated cash and balances on account, making sure items are allocated and resolved promptly.

Reporting and forecasting are a meaningful part of the position. You will prepare monthly and quarterly billing and cash collection forecasts, working with finance leadership and senior stakeholders to provide a clear view of performance and risk. You will also act as a central point of contact for billing and collections matters on key client relationships, providing regular reporting and helping resolve issues before they become blockers.

This is a collaborative role within a wider revenue team, and you will work closely with PAs, revenue assistants, and offshore operational support to maintain momentum and consistency. You will also liaise with finance colleagues across EMEA, supporting revenue and credit control activity across the region.

Compliance matters throughout. You will work within the Solicitors Accounts Rules, particularly around earmarking of funds and residual balances, and ensure VAT and local taxes are reflected correctly. You will also support write offs, time transfers and rate adjustments, keeping systems up to date and making sure the audit trail is clear.

What they’re looking for

This role suits someone with at least three years of in depth revenue control and collections experience, ideally within a law firm or professional services environment. You will be comfortable working directly with Partners, confident handling difficult conversations, and able to balance client service with commercial outcomes. Strong organisation, attention to detail, and the ability to manage competing deadlines are essential.

Experience with Elite 3E, Aderant, or a similar practice management system is important, along with strong Excel and Word skills. Knowledge of the Solicitors Accounts Rules and VAT is highly beneficial. Additional languages are helpful but not required.

If you enjoy working close to the commercial detail, partnering with senior stakeholders, and taking real ownership of billing and collections outcomes, this is a strong opportunity.

We are an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds, experiences and characteristics.

If you require any adjustments or additional support at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know.

job.title: Accounts Payable Specialist - London
job.description:
A leading international law firm is looking to hire an Accounts Payable Specialist into its London finance team.

This is a busy, detail driven role with genuine responsibility, supporting invoice processing and expense reimbursement across multiple international offices and currencies.

Working under the Finance Supervisor, with a dotted line into the International Controller, you will sit at the centre of a fast moving accounts payable function.

The work is broad and practical. You will keep the day to day engine running, but you will also be trusted with the specialist pieces that require accuracy, judgement, and confidence with stakeholders.

A big part of the role is getting complex disbursement and third party items right, particularly counsel fees and other client pay first transactions. That means reconciling fee notes against previously billed entries, ensuring the right items have been billed and collected, and then processing payments in line with the Solicitors Accounts Rules.

Alongside that, you will manage recurring monthly invoices from suppliers such as courier, cab, airline and credit card providers, chasing missing information, ensuring allocations are correct, and preparing the data so it is ready for posting.

You will also take ownership of several important month end and control focused tasks. This includes managing activity connected to the firm’s credit card programme, researching and voiding cheques or invoices when needed, investigating aged uncashed cheques and unposted payments flagged through bank reconciliations, and keeping vendor records clean and up to date. Vendor onboarding matters here too, so you will liaise with new vendors to ensure required onboarding steps are completed through the vendor system.

There is a strong service element to the role. You will be the person who responds to queries from lawyers, staff and suppliers, resolving issues efficiently and keeping communication professional. You will also support ad hoc requests for client specific accounting information and contribute to projects that improve workflow.

Compliance and confidentiality are central throughout. You will work in line with HMRC VAT requirements and the Solicitors Accounts Rules, and you will handle sensitive financial information with discretion at all times.

What they’re looking for

This role suits someone with two to three years of accounts payable experience, ideally from a legal environment where volume, deadlines and stakeholder management are part of the day to day.

You will need to be organised, analytical and accurate, with the confidence to chase missing details and the judgement to resolve issues without unnecessary escalation.

Strong Excel skills are important, and experience with systems such as Chrome River and Aderant is a real advantage.

You will also need solid communication skills, a calm approach under pressure, and the ability to work independently as well as collaboratively.

If you enjoy being the person who keeps the process moving, gets the details right first time, and builds trust across a busy firm, this is a great opportunity with real scope to grow.

job.title: Revenue Coordinator - London
job.description:
A leading international law firm is hiring a Revenue Coordinator to support the full billing and collections cycle for a portfolio of Partners and clients.

This is a hands on role where accuracy matters, deadlines matter, and the best people are the ones who can combine great stakeholder management with calm, organised execution.

You will sit close to the fee earning teams, acting as the bridge between Partners, timekeepers and finance. Your day to day will centre on preparing timely, high quality invoices, keeping WIP moving, and making sure billing activity stays aligned to client policies.

That includes reviewing proformas for misallocated time, helping correct narratives, supporting time and cost transfers, and managing write offs in line with firm policy and approval thresholds.

You will keep a close eye on rate arrangements, apply approved discounts where needed, and produce variance and write off reporting so billing decisions are properly supported.

Collections is a key part of the picture. You will monitor aged receivables, track unapplied funds, and help drive follow up after invoices are sent.

You will meet regularly with senior revenue colleagues and Partners to agree strategy, maintain clear status updates in the collections database, and flag issues early such as rate challenges, billing delays, or difficult client requests.

There is also an eBilling element. You will prepare and submit electronic invoices through client platforms, monitor submission status, and work through rejections and reductions to keep cash moving and prevent invoices from stalling.

What they’re looking for

You will need at least two years of billing experience in a law firm and the confidence to work in a demanding, high standards environment.

Strong interpersonal skills are essential, as you will be working with senior stakeholders daily. You should be comfortable managing multiple priorities, adaptable when deadlines shift, and happy to provide a consistently high level of service.

Solid Word skills and intermediate Excel are important, and flexibility for occasional overtime is expected when the workload requires it.

Working pattern and role snapshot

Standard hours are 35 per week. This is an individual contributor role reporting into the revenue leadership team, with clear scope to expand responsibilities over time based on performance and appetite to grow.

If you enjoy revenue work that is varied, stakeholder heavy, and genuinely impactful, this is a strong opportunity to build your career in a top tier environment.

job.title: Billing Coordinator (Europe) - London
job.description:
A leading international law firm is looking to hire a Billing Coordinator to support attorneys across its European offices, with day to day responsibility for keeping the billing process running smoothly, accurately, and on time.

It’s a role that sits right at the intersection of finance, client service and stakeholder management, ideal for someone who enjoys being the person that brings order, pace and clarity to a busy inventory and billing cycle.

You’ll be the link between Partners, fee earners and finance, helping matters move from “time on the system” to “invoice out the door” with minimal friction. That means understanding what each client expects, applying agreed terms and discounts, and making sure invoices are produced correctly for the relevant jurisdiction.

You’ll also be working within a regulated framework, so attention to detail matters. VAT treatment needs to be right, including reverse charge where applicable, and you’ll be mindful of AML requirements when managing billing activity across different European offices.

The work has real variety. Some days you’ll be deep in matter management, updating client and matter details, reviewing narratives, handling time transfers and edits, and supporting Partners with accrual requests.

Other days you’ll be focused on invoice production. You’ll generate proformas, issue final invoices, manage reversals and credit notes when needed, and handle the practicalities clients still ask for, such as copy invoices, statements of account, and personal disbursement invoices.

There’s also a meaningful eBilling element. You’ll help ensure matters are set up correctly for eBilling, locate and interpret billing guidelines, coordinate LEDES requirements where relevant, submit invoices through the appropriate platforms, and work with specialist colleagues to resolve rejections and queries so invoices don’t stall.

Beyond billing itself, you’ll be part of the wider effort to keep the engine running, making sure the shared inbox stays under control, supporting collections when required, helping resolve unidentified cash promptly, and responding to information requests around inventory, time and cost entries, billing reconciliations, outstanding receivables and unapplied cash. Strong Excel skills and comfort using reporting tools and dashboards will help you move quickly and confidently.

What they’re looking for

This role suits someone used to a fast moving professional environment, organised, accurate, and comfortable juggling multiple deadlines. You’ll likely have at least three years’ experience in a similar billing role within a law firm or professional services organisation, and you’ll be confident communicating with stakeholders at all levels.

Experience of European billing is helpful but not essential. Strong systems skills are important, particularly 3E and Excel, and any experience with eBilling platforms is a real advantage.

If you enjoy bringing structure to complex billing cycles, building strong relationships with busy stakeholders, and taking pride in getting invoices right first time, this is a genuinely strong opportunity.
